newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Moslems evicted from Bosnian Serb republic.
newsitem.headline: Moslems evicted from Bosnian Serb republic.

text.p: Bosnian Serbs have evicted dozens of Moslem families from a northwestern village over the past two months, defying a peace accord that demanded ethnic expulsions stop, a U.N. spokesman said on Tuesday.
More than 30 familes were ejected from their homes in Dubrava, near Bosanska Gradiska in the Bosnian Serb republic, said Alexander Ivanko, spokesman for U.N. police monitors patrolling the area.
Two families have been thrown out in the last three days and a further seven to 10 have left voluntarily, fearing for their safety, he added.
The expulsions were carried out by Bosnian Serbs who lost their homes in central Bosnia last year when the area was captured by the Moslem-led Bosnian army.
"The local authorities are implicitly supporting these evictions and are doing nothing to stop them," said Ivanko.
Tens of thousands of Moslems and Croats were forced out of north and western Bosnia by Serb terror campaigns during the 43-month war.

The peace deal of November 1995 demanded that "ethnic cleansing" halt. But the demand has been ignored, along with many other provisions of the Dayton agreement, and expulsions have continued, targeting all ethnic communities.

"We believe it is outrageous that one year after Dayton we again see minorities being thrown out of their homes in the Republika Srpska (Bosnian Serb republic) and once again we demand it stop," said Ivanko.

Foreign ministers from the United States, Europe and Russia were meeting in London this week to discuss how to improve the implementation of the Dayton deal, which has brought peace but done little to temper ethnic animosity.
